title: the bus names its host through the system device's host tool
intention: The bus names its host through the system device's host tool: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py:1057 read the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host and nowhere else, so this component names its box on every OS.
why: Akien, 2026-11-21, relayed by akiendelllinux_cc_orchestrator: "hostname should come from the system device." Folded into outline 6.6.3.7 and 2.3.7.1.5 (branch akiendelllinux/host-door-outline, 97b4ce0b7). Measured 2026-11-21: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py:1057 (_is_the_home: platform.node()) spell the host by hand, so a box with no os.uname (Windows) or a nodename the roster does not spell breaks here. Child of spanning ticket a577fd03e307 (one door names the host). Ticket 5ccc7f05c932 (READY c9824d056 on branch akiendelllinux/5ccc-host-door) builds the door, cairn/devices/system_rackmount/tools/host/host.py; this build starts after it lands on main, because the tool does not exist on main before then.
traces_to: Outline 6.6.3.7 (the hostname comes from the system device); outline 2.3.7.1.5 (the system device's host tool is one of the client tools a device publishes, the named exception to 2.3.7; a CC by-line builds, 0.4.1); outline 17.26.1 (a published client tool lives with its device); RULE 1 (the system device's public interface is the tool it publishes); Law 1 (one answer, not N re-derivations of it).
how: server.py:1057 compares against a lazy `host_name()` from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host (already short and lowercase, so the right side loses its .split/.lower). Set CAIRN_HOME_HOST by patching os.environ in-process and restoring it in finally; start no bus.

clauses.claim: an AST scan of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py finds no call to os.uname, platform.node, platform.uname or socket.gethostname, and every host name those files read comes from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host.host_name

with os.uname deleted from the os module and CAIRN_HOME_HOST set in a copied environment for the call, _is_the_home() is True for host_name().upper() + '.lan' and for an unset value, and False for 'testing-bus-not-this-box'

decisions.text: D1: each site reads the host from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host. server.py:1057 compares against a lazy `host_name()` from cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host (already short and lowercase, so the right side loses its .split/.lower). Set CAIRN_HOME_HOST by patching os.environ in-process and restoring it in finally; start no bus.

D2: the red-first proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_the_bus_names_its_host_through_the_system_device.py, one tooth per clause, PROVES keyed to this ticket; it deletes os.uname for each call and restores it in finally, and reads no live ~/.cairn.

out: every other component's host sites (siblings under a577fd03e307)
OS-family checks (platform.system, sys.platform, os.name): outline 6.6.3.7 claims the hostname only

measured.how: grep -rnE 'os\.uname\(\)|platform\.node\(\)|socket\.gethostname\(\)|platform\.uname\(\)' over cairn/ skills/ bin/ on branch akiendelllinux/5ccc-host-door (c9824d056)

measured.saw: clause 2 passes against the unbuilt code on Linux: deleting os.uname in-process cannot red it, because platform.node() falls back to socket.gethostname() there, so on this box it is a hollow green that measures nothing
measured.how: the new proof run in this ticket's worktree with the code file put back to HEAD's bytes, bin/cairn test --exec, akiendelllinux (akiendelllinux_cc_0)

builder_notes: BEFORE PROVED: akiendell_cc_0 runs this ticket's proof natively on Windows (os.uname absent there) once it is relaunched, and records that verdict on this ticket; it is clause 2's real measurement (orchestrator, 2026-11-21)
